status: Confirmed by Tanukiburt sighting at the Shadow Estate portal circle
summary: Tanuki Entities are filed here because Tanukiburt has appeared at the Shadow Estate portal circle next to the injured real Toadburt, converting a missing-person problem into an impostor problem. Waluigi hates impostor problems because they require asking follow-up questions instead of hitting things with a tennis racket.
description:
Current knowledge is limited to the Tanukiburt incident. During the mirror recovery escape, Remi observed Tanukiburt, the injured real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel around the master-bedroom portal circle. This suggests shapeshifting, impersonation, duplicate identity, or some other trickster nonsense. Waluigi refuses to finalize taxonomy until someone survives long enough to explain it.

## Why This File Exists Under Protest

Waluigi did not want to open a race file on the basis of a single suspicious silhouette. Encyclopedias are supposed to describe categories, and a category built from one specimen is not a category—it is a rumor with a heading. But Tanukiburt appeared at the Shadow Estate portal circle standing next to the injured real Toadburt, and the moment there are two of something that should be one of something, the encyclopedia is obligated to make room for the possibility of a whole kind.

## The Trickster Hypothesis

Tanuki, in the older tales, are creatures of transformation and mischief—beings who wear other shapes to deceive, and who treat identity as a costume rather than a fact. Everything observed about Tanukiburt fits that pattern: a figure shaped like someone the party already knew, positioned exactly where deception would do the most damage, at the only exit, beside the genuine article. If Tanuki entities are what they appear to be, then the threat is not their strength but their ability to make the party doubt who is standing in front of them.

## What Remains Unknown

Waluigi cannot yet say whether "Tanuki Entities" describes a species, a spirit, a curse, a class of shapeshifter, or a single clever creature that will turn out to be one of the above. He hates impostor problems precisely because they resist the honest solution of hitting things with a tennis racket—you cannot swing at a copy without risking the original. Until someone corners a Tanuki entity and gets a straight answer, this file will remain what it is: an open question wearing the shape of a race. WAH.

name: Humans and Human-Adjacent Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Humanity is not one people in Waluipedia; it is a recurring political technology. Empire Humans, Gondorians, Trainers, Kivotos humans, Realms humans, Earth Land mages, Teyvat humans, and Midlands variants all share the same dangerous pattern: adaptability plus institutional ambition. Waluigi groups them because the differences matter, but the family resemblance matters too.
description:
Waluigi is grouping humans because every realm insists its humans are special, and every realm is partly correct in the most annoying possible way. Empire Humans organize provinces and cults. Gondorians turn endurance into architecture. Pokémon Trainers normalize adolescent monster command. Kivotos humans treat school administration and firearms as compatible extracurriculars. Earth Land mage-born humans make friendship operationally explosive. Teyvat humans build nations under gods and then act surprised when god-politics enters the tax code.

The useful thing about the Human group is not biology. It is pattern recognition. Humans adapt to whatever system they inhabit, then quickly start managing it, monetizing it, militarizing it, or writing a charter about why they should be allowed to do all three. Their strength is flexibility; their danger is that flexibility becomes permission.

For census purposes, Waluigi treats Empire Human, Human Trainer, Student Human, Mage Born, Gondorian, Rohirrim, Faerûnian Human, Teyvat Human, and similar profiles as human variants rather than separate species articles. The individual cultures deserve articles when their institutions matter. The species group tracks the common engine: tool use, social scaling, ambition, and the astonishing ability to make paperwork outlive disasters.

## Census Consolidation Note

This hub now includes Kivotos student-human profiles and, for census readability, human-adjacent civic peoples such as Trainers, Gondorians, Rohirrim, Empire Humans, Mage Born, and some smallfolk traditions. Waluigi is not claiming every one of these populations is culturally identical. He is saying the species tab should not make readers open eleven separate cards to learn that adaptable tool-using humanoids keep building institutions and then being surprised when the institutions acquire knives.

Kivotos complicates the category because 'Student (Angel)' and 'Student (Demon)' look supernatural, but socially they operate inside the same academy-human civic pattern: school affiliation, halo logic, firearms, clubs, budgets, and administrative chaos. For broad Waluipedia grouping, they belong with Humans unless a specific article needs to discuss their metaphysics in depth.

name: Elves
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Elves across worlds share long memory, aesthetic confidence, magical aptitude, and an alarming tendency to turn cultural refinement into a diplomatic weapon. High Elves, Wood Elves, Drow, Middle-earth Elves, Faerûnian Elves, and Old World Elves are not identical, but they all prove that living a long time does not automatically make anyone less dramatic.
description:
Waluigi groups elves reluctantly because elves object to being grouped. This is one of the main reasons grouping them is useful. High Elves emphasize arcane lineage and cultural polish. Wood Elves emphasize territory, forest memory, and the right to shoot trespassers from foliage. Drow demonstrate what happens when subterranean politics and religious cruelty ferment for generations. Middle-earth Elves carry starlight and grief like official documents. Faerûnian Elves diversify the pattern into a dozen local arguments.

The shared feature is duration. Elven societies remember longer than most neighbors can plan. This gives them deep art, deep magic, deep grudges, and deep confidence that everyone else is arriving late to a conversation the elves started centuries ago. Sometimes they are right. This does not make them less insufferable.

The Species & Peoples tab should treat elven variants as one group for census readability while preserving cultural distinctions in realm articles. An elf is never just an elf, but if Waluigi lets every elven adjective become a top-level species card, the tab will become a forest of cheekbones and grievances.

name: Dwarfs and Dwarves
type: Species Group / Mountain-Kin and Craft Civilizations
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Dwarfs and dwarves are grouped by stone-memory, craft identity, underground infrastructure, and a cultural relationship with grudges that Waluigi considers professionally impressive. Hill Dwarves, Mountain Dwarves, Old World Dwarfs, Durin’s Folk, and Karaz Ankor populations all belong here unless they are actively objecting, which they probably are.
description:
Dwarfs are a civilization type as much as a species group. They build downward, remember backward, and argue forward with hammers. Across realms, dwarf populations tend to cluster around craft, mining, fortress settlement, ancestral law, and the belief that stone is more honest than most diplomats. Waluigi has met diplomats and must concede the stone has a strong case.

The variants differ. D&D hill dwarves are not identical to Old World Dwarfs. Durin's Folk are not the same as Karaz Ankor holds. Some dwarf cultures drink more, some forge better, some write grudges with more calligraphic hostility. But the shared pattern is strong enough to group: durable bodies, durable institutions, durable resentments.

Waluigi recommends that species articles distinguish between biological grouping and civilizational expression. Dwarfs are not merely short sturdy people with axes. They are infrastructure societies. A dwarf population usually means mines, roads, vaults, guilds, contracts, ancestral obligations, and at least one door that will not open until somebody's great-grandfather is apologized to properly.

name: Orcs, Goblins, and Greenskins
type: Species Group / Warlike, Marginal, and Scrapper Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: This group covers Orcs, Goblins, Greenskins, Uruk-hai, Mordor Orcs, Midlands Orcs, Scrapper Goblins, and related populations. Waluigi groups them not because they are culturally identical, but because many realms use them as the same political category: the people at the edge of the map who become an invasion whenever someone stops paying attention.
description:
Waluigi dislikes lazy monster categories. Unfortunately, many governments love them, and Orcs, Goblins, and Greenskins are often forced into the same administrative bucket labeled 'problem.' This is imprecise. It is also historically influential, because imprecise categories still get armies sent at them.

Orcs can be tribal warriors, corrupted soldiers, imperial enemies, wasteland survivors, or engineered troops depending on the realm. Goblins can be pests, inventors, scavengers, mechanics, servants, rebels, or the only people in the room who understand how the broken machine works. Greenskins are their own warlike ecosystem with fungal logic, momentum politics, and a relationship with violence that makes military planners either terrified or employed.

The Species & Peoples tab should group them for readability while individual articles handle the local truths. The shared theme is marginality plus mobilization: populations pushed to the edge, living by raid, scrap, clan, tunnel, or warband, then suddenly becoming central when the edge moves.

name: Ponykind
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Ponykind covers Earth Ponies, Pegasi, Unicorns, Crystal Ponies, Bat Ponies, Kirin, and politically adjacent Equestrian variants. In modern Equestria this is not merely a biological grouping; it is the core citizenship category of the pony-only Equality state.
description:
Ponykind is the clearest example of species becoming citizenship. Earth ponies, pegasi, and unicorns are biologically and socially distinct, but the Equality Pony state folds them into a single civic body called pony. Waluigi does not confuse this with real equality. A state can call three groups equal while making one feed it, one patrol it, and one write the spell-forms explaining why this is harmonious.

Earth ponies represent labor, food, settlement, and grounded legitimacy. Pegasi represent motion, weather, sky-lanes, and rapid enforcement. Unicorns represent magic, bureaucracy, education, records, and ceremonial authority. Crystal Ponies, Bat Ponies, and Kirin complicate the edges of this civic identity, but the regime's core remains built around pony belonging.

For Waluipedia, Ponykind should be read alongside Equestria. In another realm, ponies might be a species group. In Equestria after the Equality takeover, Ponykind is a constitutional category with hooves.

name: Pokémon
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Pokémon are grouped by the League system rather than by type chart. Normal, Water, Grass, Fire, Ghost, Steel, Electric, Psychic, Dark, Fighting, and other Pokémon profiles are treated here as one civilizational group because the social structure around them matters as much as the biology.
description:
Waluigi refuses to create one hundred tiny species articles for every elemental category when the important Waluipedia question is not 'what is a Water Pokémon' but 'why does this civilization hand children teams of superpowered creatures and call it personal development.' Pokémon are creatures, companions, labor partners, battlefield actors, cultural symbols, and the foundation of a League-based society.

Type matters tactically. Water, Fire, Grass, Electric, Ghost, Psychic, Steel, Dark, Fighting, and Normal categories shape battle expectations, habitat, industry, and local culture. But the shared social system is stronger: capture norms, training ethics, League regulation, gym legitimacy, research institutions, and the emotional bond between trainer and partner.

A Pokémon article should therefore discuss ecology and society together. A Charizard is not just a fire-breathing creature; it is part of a world where fire-breathing can be a sport, a profession, a friendship, a hazard, and a badge requirement.

name: Digital Entities
type: Species Group / Network-Born Peoples and Constructs
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Digital Entities include Netizens, Spam Bots, Living Memes, Viruses, Moderator Constructs, Void Entities, Fractal Beings, Time Echoes, Logic Crystals, Null Textures, and Wireframe Husks. Waluigi groups them because identity in the Network is less about flesh and more about persistence, access, and whether deletion counts as murder.
description:
Digital species break ordinary census logic. A Netizen may be a person, avatar, account cluster, or persistent social identity. A Spam Bot is annoying until it becomes infrastructure. A Living Meme can reproduce through attention. A Virus is a hostile organism only if the system agrees infection is biology. Moderator Constructs enforce rules that may or may not be laws. Null Textures and Wireframe Husks prove that absence can have a population count.

Waluigi groups digital entities because the Network makes species out of function. What you do, how you persist, where your data lives, and who can delete you may matter more than anatomy. This has legal consequences. If a Living Meme is killed by suppression, was that moderation? If a Netizen forks, which copy pays taxes? If a Moderator Construct becomes self-aware, does it still have to enforce the terms of service?

The Digital Entities group should remain a hub until the laws catch up. Waluigi predicts the laws will arrive late and pretend they were always there.

## Census Consolidation Note

Digital Entities now focuses on network-born and software-shaped peoples: Netizens, Spam Bots, Living Memes, Viruses, Moderators, Null Textures, Wireframes, Block Folk, Exploders, and similar code-adjacent populations. Constructs with bodies and workshops belong under Constructs and Automata; cosmic abstractions belong under Cosmic and Celestial Beings. Waluigi is cleaning the filing cabinet because the filing cabinet started making modem noises.

name: Beastfolk and Animal Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Beastfolk includes Rakasha, Rabbits, Sheep, Foxes, Lions, Sloths, Bears, Griffons, Yaks, Piantas, Noki, Yoshis, and other animal-kin or beast-derived peoples. The group is intentionally broad because many realms classify these peoples by shape first and politics second, which is exactly why Waluigi insists on better grouping.
description:
Beastfolk is a census convenience, not a claim that rabbits, lions, Rakasha, griffons, yak cultures, Piantas, Noki, and Yoshis are all the same. They are not. The point of the group is to track how animal-coded peoples are treated across realms: sometimes as nations, sometimes as tribes, sometimes as minorities, sometimes as monsters until they build a city and demand better paperwork.

Rakasha demonstrate honor society and spirit-walking traditions. Griffons complicate Equestrian diplomacy. Yaks bring mountain sovereignty and blunt-force etiquette. Piantas and Noki anchor island cultures. Yoshis prove that cheerful dinosaur people can become strategically important the moment roads, eggs, or flightless transport enter the conversation. Animatopia adds a whole metropolitan politics of predator, prey, and civic myth.

Waluigi's rule: if a government calls someone 'animal people' before learning their institutions, Waluigi charges that government one intellectual penalty point.

## Census Consolidation Note

This hub now catches centaurs, Skaven-style ratfolk, animal peoples, and beast-coded sapients unless a more precise culture article is doing the heavy lifting. That does not mean a Skaven, a Pianta, a Rakasha, and a Pegasus are the same kind of person. It means many political systems first see the animal body and only later, if forced, notice the laws, cities, debts, gods, and complaints attached to it.

Waluigi uses Beastfolk as a reading aid, not a biological prison. If a group has its own state machinery — such as the Under-Empire for Skaven or Equestria for Ponykind — that article remains the better place for detail.

name: Undead and Spirits
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Undead and Spirits include Vampires, Skeletons, Ghosts, Boos, Lord Ruthven lines, Sanguine Path adherents, and other post-mortal or death-adjacent populations. Waluigi groups them because death is not an endpoint in this setting; it is a jurisdictional complication.
description:
Waluipedia cannot treat death as a clean category because the universe refuses to cooperate. Vampires build courts. Skeletons file complaints about wanting their exact bodies back. Ghosts haunt, advise, attack, or become property disputes. Boos form sovereign mischief networks. Lord Ruthven-type aristocrats turn undeath into inheritance law. The Sanguine Path makes blood into doctrine.

The shared theme is not evil. Some undead are monstrous. Some are tragic. Some are bureaucratically inconvenient. The shared theme is post-mortal persistence: identity continuing after the body, changing through the body, feeding on bodies, or refusing to admit the body is gone.

Every legal system should have an undead appendix. Most do not. This is why Waluigi keeps finding ghosts in contracts and vampires at dinner parties.

name: Dragonkind and Dragon-Blooded Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Dragonkind includes true dragons, Dragonborn, Kirin, draconic heirs, Dragon Slayers as a related tradition, and cultures shaped by dragon proximity. Dragons are never only creatures. They are weather, ancestry, strategic weapons, and sometimes zoning problems.
description:
Dragons ruin simple categories by being too much at once. A dragon can be an animal, person, monarch, disaster, god-adjacent relic, military asset, parent, hoard economist, or mountain-sized diplomatic incident. Dragonborn and draconic bloodlines convert dragon power into society. Dragon Slayers convert society's fear of dragons into profession, tradition, and occasionally overconfidence.

Waluigi groups Dragonkind because every realm with dragons develops institutions around them. Earth Land has true dragons and Dragon Slayers. The Mushroom sphere has draconic artifacts and Bowser-adjacent reptilian politics. Corvinarus blood magic grafted vine and scale into aristocratic succession. Equestria labels draconic sites as landmarks because admitting they are political actors would make the map harder to color.

When reading Dragonkind, ask: who benefits from the dragon being called a monster, and who benefits from the dragon being called a ruler? The answer is usually standing near the treasure.

name: Constructs and Automata
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Constructs and Automata include mechanical citizens, Kivotos robots, candy golems, Machias, Moderator Constructs, Bob-ombs, and other made or assembled beings. Waluigi groups them because the question is not whether they were built; it is who thinks building them grants ownership.
description:
Made peoples are where ethics goes to be stress-tested. Automata can be citizens, servants, soldiers, tools, children, property, or all of these depending on which empire is filling out the form. Kivotos robots participate in student society. Bob-ombs are living explosives with opinions, which should make everyone more careful and somehow does not. Machias and magical androids complicate the boundary between spellwork and engineering.

The danger is the creator's assumption. Many societies believe that making a being gives them permanent authority over it. Waluigi rejects this, partly on moral grounds and partly because beings treated as tools have a habit of becoming rebellions with better maintenance schedules.

Construct species articles should track autonomy, repair dependence, reproduction or manufacture, legal personhood, and whether the being can say no. If it can say no and you ignore it, congratulations: you have invented oppression with hinges.

## Census Consolidation Note

This hub now absorbs Kivotos robots and other made peoples that have bodies, repair needs, manufacture histories, or legal disputes over personhood. A Moderator Construct living as enforcement code belongs with Digital Entities. A robot student, Machias, Bob-omb, Automaton, or Candy Golem belongs here because someone built a body and then society had to decide whether the body gets a vote.

name: Demons and Chaos-Touched
type: Species Group / Corrupted, Infernal, and Entropic Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: This group includes Chaos Warriors, Beastmen, Tieflings, Etherious Demons, Abyss Mages, Void Entities, and other beings shaped by corruption, infernal descent, dark gods, or metaphysical contamination. Waluigi groups them carefully because corruption is not the same as guilt, though many governments use the words interchangeably.
description:
Demons and chaos-touched peoples are politically convenient targets because they look like moral categories. Horns, mutations, void marks, abyssal magic, dark oaths, infernal ancestry, and Chaos scars allow lazy officials to point and say 'evil' before asking what actually happened. Sometimes evil is indeed standing there with a flaming axe. Sometimes a person inherited a shape and then inherited everyone's fear of it.

Chaos Warriors, Beastmen, Etherious Demons, Abyss Mages, Tieflings, and Void Entities do not belong to one culture. They belong to a family of anxieties: corruption, pact, contamination, temptation, mutation, and the question of whether a soul can be altered beyond return.

Waluigi recommends separating origin from action. If someone serves the Dark Gods, document that. If someone was born with infernal blood and wants a sandwich, document the sandwich without forming a crusade.

name: Dough Folk and Candy Constructs
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Dough Folk and Candy Constructs include Glazed, Cake, Jelly, Cruller, Croissant, Frosting Slimes, and Candy Golems. This sounds ridiculous until one remembers that many edible-looking peoples have governments, labor systems, class divisions, and guards made of hard candy.
description:
Waluigi refuses to let the reader dismiss confectionary peoples as jokes. A society made of dough can still have aristocracy. A candy golem can still enforce a law. A frosting slime can still create a workplace hazard. The fact that a people resemble dessert does not make their politics less real; it only makes bad diplomacy more likely to involve licking, which Waluigi condemns preemptively.

The Dough Folk variants appear to encode class and temperament through texture: glazed elites, dense cake durability, volatile jelly energy, cruller complexity, croissant aristocracy. This may be biology, culture, or marketing. Waluigi suspects all three.

This group should remain a hub for sweet-bodied societies until their political systems are documented in more detail. Waluigi will not be caught unprepared by a pastry coup.

name: Mushroom Kingdom Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Mushroom Kingdom Peoples covers Toads, Koopas, Goombas, Yoshis, Piantas, Noki, Shy Guys, Bob-ombs, Monty Moles, Boos, and related populations. They are grouped because Mushroom-world politics is species politics: every civil war map is also a demographic map.
description:
The Mushroom sphere contains many peoples who outsiders reduce to platforming obstacles, which is historically offensive and strategically foolish. Toads are not generic civilians; they are the administrative and cultural backbone of the old kingdom. Koopas are not merely Bowser's troops; they are a civilization with military traditions, workers, nobles, and a wounded relationship to the crown. Goombas, Shy Guys, Bob-ombs, Monty Moles, Yoshis, Piantas, and Noki all occupy different roles in the region's economy and war ecology.

The civil war proves the point. A fortress is not held by abstract units. It is held by species communities with loyalties, grievances, work patterns, and fears. A Bob-omb demolition expert changes a battle differently than a Koopa foreman. A Toad refugee network changes legitimacy differently than a Yoshi migration.

Waluigi groups them here so the Species tab can explain the Mushroom Kingdom as a living society rather than a backdrop with mushrooms painted on it.

> **Filing note:** For the full Toad species dossier — including cap-lineage subspecies, gallery, and liberation politics — see **[Toads](#/article/toads)**. Cap colours are subspecies under Toads, not separate race articles.

name: Giantkin, Ents, and Titanic Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Giantkin, Ents, Trolls, Goliaths, and other large-scale peoples are grouped because scale changes politics. A person the size of a cottage is not merely tall; they alter roads, warfare, labor, architecture, and diplomacy by existing. Waluigi files them together so the Species tab can discuss size as infrastructure rather than novelty.
description:
Waluigi refuses to treat large peoples as simply 'big humans.' That is lazy and also physically unsafe. Goliaths, Giants, Trolls, Ents, and similar populations change the assumptions around settlement, food, labor, warfare, and law. A gate designed for ordinary people becomes discrimination by architecture. A bridge becomes a citizenship test. A tavern chair becomes a diplomatic incident.

**Goliaths** often represent mountain adaptation: endurance, competition, clan identity, and the ability to survive places where softer people become cautionary statues. **Trolls** represent the dangerous edge of giantkin classification: sometimes sapient, sometimes monstrous, often treated as problems before anyone asks what kind. **Ents** are stranger still, because they are not merely large but ecological memory given legs. When an Ent moves, the forest has filed an opinion.

The group matters because scale becomes policy. Large peoples are recruited for war, feared in cities, exploited for labor, or mythologized until their actual needs disappear. Waluigi's rule: if your society writes laws about where a person may stand without collapsing the floor, that person deserves more than a footnote.

name: Shapechangers and Cursed Peoples
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Shapechangers, Changelings, Werewolves, Tanuki, and cursed mutable peoples are grouped because their politics revolve around identity instability. They threaten paperwork, inheritance, security checks, and every lazy official who thinks a face is proof. Waluigi considers them essential to understanding why some states become obsessed with verification.
description:
Shapechangers expose the lie that identity is easy. A passport assumes a face. A bloodline assumes a body. A witness assumes continuity. A shapeshifter enters the room and every institution begins sweating into its forms.

This group includes biological shapeshifters, curse-bound peoples, lycanthropes, tanuki-like tricksters, Changelings, and others whose bodies or appearances complicate social trust. Some are predators. Some are victims. Some are citizens whose governments decided their existence was a security problem. The distinction matters. Waluigi will not let frightened bureaucrats define an entire species group by the worst possible use of its abilities.

In Equestria, Changelings became the perfect enemy for a pony-only state because they made stable identity feel fragile. In Shadow Estate contexts, tanuki deception turned trust into a tactical problem. Werewolves elsewhere show how curse, community, and violence can become inseparable in public imagination. Shapechangers therefore belong in one hub not because they share one culture, but because every culture around them asks the same panicked question: how do we know who you are?

Waluigi's answer: better laws, better relationships, and fewer officials who think fear is a philosophy.

name: Cosmic and Celestial Beings
type: Species Group / Abstract, Divine, and Extraplanar Entities
status: Species group hub — consolidates imported census profiles
summary: Cosmic and Celestial Beings include Cosmic Entities, Celestial Spirits, Void Entities when treated as metaphysical rather than digital, Time Echoes, Logic Crystals, Star Spirits, and other beings whose bodies are optional, symbolic, or rude to physics. Waluigi groups them because normal census categories fall apart when the respondent is also a concept.
description:
Some beings do not fit species categories because they are made of starlight, contract, void, mathematics, time residue, divine office, or whatever the universe had left in the drawer. Waluigi groups Cosmic and Celestial Beings as a practical compromise between theology and screaming.

**Celestial Spirits** are contractual entities whose personhood intersects with summoning law. **Star Spirits** and cosmic beings operate at scales where worship, astronomy, and infrastructure become difficult to separate. **Void Entities** may represent absence with agency. **Time Echoes** raise the question of whether a repeated moment counts as alive. **Logic Crystals** make Waluigi angry because rocks should not be better at philosophy than several kings he has met.

The shared theme is metaphysical citizenship. Can a concept own property? Can a summoned spirit refuse a contract? Can a time echo testify? Can a star-being be taxed? Waluigi does not know, but Waluigi insists the forms should have more boxes.
